contentBlocks.body: SQL injection happens when user input is pasted into SQL text, so the input can change the query's structure. With `"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'"`, a name of `x' OR '1'='1` returns every user, and worse inputs can modify or drop data. It is still one of the most common serious web vulnerabilities.

Parameters work because the database parses the SQL text first and receives the values separately; a value can never become syntax, whatever quotes or semicolons it contains. As a bonus, the same query text is reused for every value, so the plan cache gets hits instead of compiling a new plan per distinct literal. Escaping quotes by hand is not a substitute; it misses encodings and edge cases.

Parameters can only stand in for values, never for identifiers or keywords: table names, column names, ASC/DESC. When users choose the sort column, map their input through an allow-list of known column names and fall back to a default. Never pass the raw string through, even "just for ORDER BY".
Defense in depth: connect with a database login that has only the permissions the app needs (no db_owner, no DROP), so even a missed injection has a limited blast radius.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Build a parameterized search like a Dapper or ADO.NET repository would. Base query: `SELECT id, name, city, age FROM users`. Add conditions in this order when the filter is not null: name = @pN, city = @pN, age >= @pN (N counts up from 0), joined with AND after WHERE. Append ORDER BY using sortBy only if it is one of name, age, city; otherwise ORDER BY id. Return { sql, params }. Values must never appear in the SQL text.
Why does a parameterized query stop `x' OR '1'='1` from returning every row?

choices: The driver deletes every quote character from the input
The value is sent separately from the already-parsed SQL, so it is compared as a plain string and never parsed as SQL
Parameters are encrypted before being sent
The database refuses strings that contain OR
payload.answer: The value is sent separately from the already-parsed SQL, so it is compared as a plain string and never parsed as SQL
payload.explanation: The query looks for a user literally named x' OR '1'='1. Nothing is stripped or escaped; the structure is simply fixed before the value arrives.

knowledgeItems.prompt: A grid lets users sort by any column via ?sort=... in the URL. How should the ORDER BY be built?

choices: Pass it as a parameter: ORDER BY @sort
Map the input through an allow-list of known column names, defaulting to id
Concatenate it after escaping single quotes
Reject requests containing a semicolon and concatenate the rest
payload.answer: Map the input through an allow-list of known column names, defaulting to id
payload.explanation: Identifiers cannot be parameters (ORDER BY @sort sorts by a constant value, which does nothing). Blocklists and escaping miss cases; an allow-list cannot be bypassed.
